_comment: docs/architecture.md decision 3: what Component B's `member` column means per bank (b_basis). c_basis (added 2026-09-21) is the same idea for Component C -- trivial_region (mandate mirrors recipient status once B is resolved, since the bank's own recipient set is already regionally defined), spell_based (needs a real dated mandate_spells.csv), computed (derived from other membership lists, e.g. BADEA's AU-not-Arab-League rule). Other fields from architecture.md's fuller sketch (window_rule, nonaccrual_bars_new_lending, annual_report_parser) are added only once the phase that needs them starts, not guessed here.

banks.b_basis_note: Virtually every sovereign state is a World Bank Group member; the IBRD/IDA recipient split is an income-window question, not a separate borrowing-member list.
banks.b_basis_source: docs/architecture.md §2 (D notes: "IBRD/IDA status comes from OGHIST plus thresholds"); CLAUDE.md Known Traps
banks.c_basis_note: IBRD's mandate is global membership itself; no separate geography to check once B is resolved.
banks.c_basis_source: docs/architecture.md §2: "Trivially 1 for banks whose recipient list is already regional"
banks.d_basis_note: Income-window criterion comes from OGHIST.xlsx's country income-classification history.
banks.d_basis_source: docs/architecture.md §2: "IBRD/IDA status comes from OGHIST plus thresholds"

banks.b_basis_note: Same reasoning as IBRD -- some IDA members are donors, not recipients (e.g. the US), but that split is Component D (operational cutoff), not a separate B list.
banks.b_basis_source: docs/architecture.md §2 (D notes); CLAUDE.md Known Traps ("Blend countries are eligible for both arms")

banks.b_basis_note: AfDB's 54 Regional Member Countries recipient set -- covers both the ordinary and concessional (ADF) windows identically; ADF was briefly its own bank code (2026-09-24 - 2026-09-28) and is merged back here, see docs/coding_decisions.md, 2026-09-28.
banks.b_basis_source: docs/architecture.md §2: "Borrowing-member list (IDB, AsDB, CDB, AfDB, IsDB, CAF, AIIB, NDB)"
banks.c_basis_note: AfDB's recipient set (recipient_status.csv) is already the 54 regional members; non-regional shareholders are already excluded at B.
banks.d_basis_note: No further internal income-based sub-window at the eligibility level -- window_ok=1 for any confirmed regional recipient; the ordinary/concessional distinction is a commitments-level breakdown (build_afdb_window_breakdown.py), not a separate eligibility window.

banks.c_basis_note: AsDB's recipient set (the 50 DMCs) is already regional; developed regional members (Japan, Australia, etc.) are already non_borrowing at B.
banks.d_basis_note: Same reasoning as AfDB: one combined "AsDB" bank code (no separate AsDF, decision 2 open), and Component B's DMC/developed-member split already does the real work of distinguishing recipients. window_ok=1 for any confirmed DMC recipient.

banks.c_basis_note: IDB's 26 borrowing members are already exactly the Latin America/Caribbean region.
banks.d_basis_note: window_ok = 1 unconditionally; IDB has no income-based lending window distinct from Component B.
banks.d_basis_source: docs/architecture.md §2: "Every other bank is 1, with source 'no formal income window'"

banks.b_basis_note: The real recipient restriction is EBRD's countries-of-operations status, which is Component C (see docs/coding_decisions.md, 2026-09-21, "EBRD's Date joined is Component B not C" -- Egypt/Morocco show a 1991 shareholder date but only became countries of operations in 2012).
banks.b_basis_source: docs/architecture.md §2: "Membership only, with the recipient restriction carried by C (EBRD...)"
banks.c_basis_note: Needs mandate_spells.csv -- EBRD's countries-of-operations timeline. Not a trivial-region bank precisely because this is the one place its real recipient restriction lives.
banks.d_basis_note: window_ok = 1 unconditionally; no formal income window.

banks.b_basis_note: member = 1 always; EIB's real restriction outside the EU is its external lending mandate, a Component C question.
banks.b_basis_source: docs/architecture.md §2: "No membership condition (EIB outside the EU, BADEA...)"
banks.c_basis_note: Needs eu_membership.csv (in-EU case) and mandate_spells.csv sourced from EUR-Lex External Lending Mandate decisions (external case).
banks.d_basis_note: window_ok = 1 unconditionally; no formal income window.

banks.c_basis_note: IsDB's mandate is OIC membership itself, already the B criterion.
banks.d_basis_note: Same reasoning as AfDB/AsDB: one combined "IsDB" bank code covers both concessional (ISFD) and ordinary windows, and IsDB's own material ties concessional terms (not eligibility itself) to income tier. window_ok=1 for any confirmed IsDB recipient.

banks.c_basis_note: CAF's recipient set (recipient_status.csv) is already Latin America/Caribbean; Spain/Portugal are already unknown, not borrowing, at B.
banks.d_basis_note: window_ok = 1 unconditionally; no formal income window.

banks.c_basis_note: CDB's 19 borrowing members are already exactly the Caribbean region.
banks.d_basis_note: window_ok = 1 unconditionally; no formal income window.

banks.b_basis_note: 111 approved members; Germany and the UK will never borrow (CLAUDE.md Known Traps).
banks.c_basis_note: AIIB's own FAQ states the actual rule directly, no income or regional gate: "AIIB may provide or facilitate financing to any member, or any agency, instrumentality or political subdivision thereof, or any entity or enterprise operating in the territory of a member... Prospective members will only be eligible for financing after they become a member." Supersedes an earlier, wrong guess (architecture.md's "member AND NOT high-income" framing, itself contradicted twice by real observed lending -- docs/coding_decisions.md, 2026-09-21).
banks.c_basis_source: https://www.aiib.org/en/projects/apply/faq/index.html ("Who can apply for financing?"), supplied directly by the user 2026-09-21
banks.d_basis_note: window_ok = 1 unconditionally; no formal income window.

banks.b_basis_note: member = 1 always; BADEA lends to non-members. Real restriction is AU-member-and-not-Arab-League, a Component C computation.
banks.b_basis_source: docs/architecture.md §2: "No membership condition (EIB outside the EU, BADEA, which lends to non-members)"
banks.c_basis_note: AU member AND NOT Arab League member, from au_membership.csv and arab_league_membership.csv.
banks.c_basis_source: docs/architecture.md §2: "BADEA is computed: AU member and not Arab League member"
banks.d_basis_note: window_ok = 1 unconditionally; no formal income window.

banks.b_basis_note: "Prospective members" admitted by the Board of Governors but not yet acceded are not members (CLAUDE.md Known Traps) -- accession_dates.csv already applies this; recipient-status research still needed on top of bare membership.
banks.c_basis_note: NDB has no non-borrowing bloc found (docs/coding_decisions.md, 2026-09-21) and no regional restriction beyond membership itself.
banks.d_basis_note: window_ok = 1 unconditionally; no formal income window.

banks.b_basis_note: Not in architecture.md's table -- CABEI was added in session 2, after that doc was written. Classified by analogy: CABEI has regional (Central American) founding members and non-regional members (e.g. Taiwan, Argentina, Colombia, Cuba, Mexico, Dominican Republic, South Korea, Spain), the same shareholder-vs-borrower shape as AIIB/IDB.
banks.c_basis_note: CABEI's 8 regional borrowing members are already exactly Central America/Panama/Dominican Republic/Belize.
banks.d_basis_note: window_ok = 1 unconditionally; no formal income window.
